My favorite lightweight game. Its not demanding at all, as you can see. This will for ever be one of my favorite games even if its small and doesn't get updated.

It's fun, it runs well, it looks great, and though there's not a *massive* amount of variety (atleast 5 hours in) in terms of abilities/upgrades to choose mid-game, the different characters & weapons make the runs *feel* different.

Also it's £4~ and I've got 5 hours out of it (so far), like, what more do you want.

an interesting take on the vampire survivors formula
specifically you need to attack manually instead of the game doing it for you as the game is a twin stick shooter.
the game functions identically to VS whre you kill enemies, collect the XP they drop, and survive until 20 minutes have passed, except, again, you have a gun
you have a selection of different characters you play each with their own unique gimmick, and a starting weapon which also have unique gimmicks to them and do compliment certain characters along with work wonders with specific abilities
not the most deepest in terms of amount of content you get compared to VS with only 3 maps to play on and after a while you will pretty much know all the upgrades you'll get, but still very replayable as the game has increasing levles of "darkness" which modify future runs to become increasingly harder
not the deepest amount of content but it is fuffiling and satisfying to play, and is cheap, so i'd reccomend
Way too fun. The customization is insane, and the buildcrafting is real. One of the most fun games i've played, and also one of the most replayable.

7/10 - Fun for a bit, but gets old super quickly. Want to enjoy a fun build idea you had? Chances are unless it's a min-max of a few of the exact same skills, it probably won't keep up with how bullet spongey the enemies get.

While this game is pretty rudimentary for an autobattler, it's definitely more interactive than the other ones as, for the most part, you want to be manually aiming for all your shots. I think if there was more a variety of enemy, specifically those who shoot bullets and a limited dodge button (technically there is one but there's only one character that can use it as her special ability), I think this game would be a perfect time killer.

As of now, there's a little imbalance in some of the strategies, like how dual smgs and Abby or Spark is just an instant win. On top of that, some status effects aren't very useful, making some characters very weak compared to the rest of the characters, such as Scarlett or Yuki. I think a lot of these can be remedy with patches and aren't a foundational pillar of the game that's fundamentally broken.

While there's some issues I have with the game, I still think it's rather good for what it is, especially with its price point of $3 USD. If your reading this and haven't bought the game, I'd recommend you play it, it is very fun.

This is definitely a great entry in the genre (Magic Survival, Vampire Survivors, Gothic Survival..)
The main innovation being that this time, you have to actively use your weapon instead of it activating on cooldown.
This makes the game more interesting and less passive imo.

My feedback so far :

+ seems like amazing value for the price tag
+ interesting ideas added to the formula (active weapons, perk paths)
+ massive, satisfying power creep that starts instantly. no boring first few minutes
+ highly synergistic upgrades
+ lovely visuals
+ atmosphere
+ just solid fun

- controller support is a bit basic
- some weapons could use more oomph in both sounds and sfx, like the shotgun
- a few sprites are still a bit rough, like Lilith's spirits

Things I would love to see added :
* controller button prompts
* controller deadzone (choosing a perk feels a bit off to me)
* screenshake slider
* ways to unlock color palettes
* a way to tweak or remove the turning speed of your character when using a controller
* more juice / feedback / effects!

I really love this game so far and cannot wait to see what it grows into!
This game has a unique style and charm but it's not too alienated from other roguelikes. It's an awesome challenge but very rewarding.

This game is awesome! A more active aproach this wave of power trippy survival bullet hells like Vampire Survivors. I loved it. Couldn't put the game down.

Overall, I don't have anything bad to talk about this game other then crossbow being extremely weak. And for the price this game goes, this is just insane value!

20 Minutes Till Dawn is a delightful little rogue-lite to sink 20 minutes or hours at a time into. The main gameplay consists of destroying massive hordes of enemies that endlessly encroach on your position. After each run you gain currency based on your performance which is then used to obtain more characters, weapons, and skill upgrades. The different characters and weapons all greatly influence the gameplay variance, changing the possible synergies that you can obtain in a run which keeps the game fresh as you switch up your playstyle frequently.

It is really impressive just how many enemies, projectiles, and other effects are present while still not clogging up the screen, distracting the player, or breaking the game. I have not encountered any bugs, technical issues, or frame rate drops; flawless in those regards.

The pixel art is very pretty, the gameplay loop is addicting, the particle FX are amazing albeit sometimes overwhelming, and the combat is FUN. I'd recommend this to anyone who likes rogue-lites. I'd have been happy with my purchase even if I got it for $20-$30 but I got it on sale for just a few dollars, definitely worth the money.

A fun and rewarding rogue-lite, 20 Minutes Till Dawn is one of those games that renews your interest in the genre. I play on both PC and Steam Deck, and can say I have not run into any issues, performance-wise or other. The combat is fluid, the music is nice, and the characters are neat. As you would expect, there is not yet much of a story, as is with a lot of rogue-lites, but the game feels alive nonetheless.

If you enjoy games where you turn into the bullet hell, then this game is for you.

Consider this abandonware. If you can bother keeping the mobile updated but you can't do the same for Steam, take it off the store pages until you do. Generating income off one that's essentially dead while the other platform still gets updated is scummy.

Willing to reconsider if we ever see anything again, but highly doubtful.

Highly recommended

Short:
+ very nice pixel art and color scheme
+ fun and unique character abilities
+ nice skills
+ 32 hours entertainment for 5€ (100% worth it)
- random skills (I know roguelike does this and it's fine - it's really the only "negative" point I can make)

Long:
I usually don't like roguelike games because of the random factor but this game really got me with the unique characters, skills and the wonderful artstyle. Maybe my first steam game I did 100% with all achivements. It can be frustrating but also so rewarding when you just overkill the whole screen.
Even if it is a shooter you can kind of be a summoner which I really love to play (Batgun <3).

This game is litterally impossible. You can beat it a couple times with the most broken of combos... but that's it... if you try and step out of the box and try some new fun build.. you're dead in 5 seconds. You can't even have a little fun trying something new. You just die.

Overall the 1st little bit is fun. But after you discover the busted combos and beat the game a time or two you realize that this whole game is balanced JUST around those combos. Every other level up choice is a trap. Don't buy this game until they get this aweful balance under control. Its not worth the effort. And in its current state this game is fun for maybe an hour or two. But no more.

$3 for 21 straight hours of fun.

If you like Vampire Survivors for how crazy it scales up, and other twin stick shooters, this is a game for you. Stylish, plays well. Feels like a finished game despite the Early Access tag, really!

I'm not sure if this is a hot take or not, but visually and by what I've experienced, I enjoy this game more than Vampire Survivors. Then again I never played that game yet, but if you're looking for a fun, good roguelike, this is definitely one imo

If you like to watch paint dry you will love this game.
Unfortunately the game is just a lot shallower than other contestants in the genre.
There isn't really any challenge to the game to keep you playing which leaves a disappointing aftertaste.

This game is amazing and you should buy it, however, I have some minor complaints. A near perfect run is based on what upgrades you get at what time. Some upgrades allow for stat increases with number of kills, heals or minutes since the upgrade was acquired. It can be very frustrating basing a build off of these stats and just not getting the upgrade every level. I'm not sure what would be a fix for that, I know it's part of the game, but it does annoy me. Second, the pre-game upgrade of having the two stones fly around you that pushes away enemies has no way of signalling when it is going to pulse. This has resulted many times in me walking around and preparing to dodge monsters, only to have them be pushed another direction, hitting me and losing me health or a shield. There should be a sparkle indicating a pulse is coming, otherwise they do more harm than good.
Such an amazing survival game. It has multiple characters, multiple weapons, multiple abilities and multiple runes to choose from.

For a smaller rouge like. It does its job well. Different characters offer different upgrades, while different weapons offer unique combinations. With different stages offering different enemies and bosses to fight. It adds just that extra little sprinkle of content to help prevent the gameplay from getting stale.

Do you like survivor games, but want to be able to aim where you want? That's this! It's got multiple characters with their own skills. It's got many weapons, upgrades, AND a talent tree! Stop reading this and go play the demo "10 minutes till dawn".

I enjoy the gameplay style, and the artwork/feel of the game is done extremely well. I like the fact there is a "story" aspect tied to the 'last XX minutes to win the round' feel. I hope as the game develops, they introduce more weapon styles and mostly the story. Who are these characters, why are they out in the woods/temple/etc. and trying to survive until dawn. Are they scouts, part of a group and the only survivor trying to return home to tell their families? What are the monsters after them and why?

My friend showed me this game in the demo version and it looked pretty fun and so I bought the full version when it came out and so far, i'm enjoying it. It has loads of different weapon choices and characters with different abilities. The rune buffs are pretty cool as well in giving you a starting edge in higher levels. Though I did think that it was a little too free right off the bat since you have a lot of the characters unlocked immediately. That's really the only i guess con to this game is that the beginning is almost free but still enjoyable. I do feel like some characters are busted in certain cases so that's why I thought you wouldn't have the characters right off the bat.

Kinda addicting once you start playing and you get far in each run and you feel like you can do better and finding the right combination of skills that work for each level. As well as the satisfaction of clearing hordes of enemies at once. Love the game and would recommend
Fun game, but sadly the pc version has been abandoned. Mobile is Ad riddled slop, and im not paying more money to play on a worse platform.

Great entry into the early vampire survivors clone genre, it has a bit more player control than others, far more visual polish, perhaps a bit less focus on making quirky builds, but it's a fun game that is fun to 100%.

It's really hard not to recommend a game when the price tag is so low. That being said, this game is a lot of fun. It's got (as you have read, I'm certain) a Vampire Survivors vibe to it, but instead of passive attacks, you point and click (or press space to auto-target) to shoot the enemies swarming you. I have yet to play enough to get really OP runs and just annihilate everything, but regardless, I am enjoying the process of getting there.
